      Checkpoints sync to one remote - right now "origin", and your first push to
      your branch's own remote takes it over. `entire status` shows where.
      Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin one yourself.
    
    Once the destination is settled the note shrinks: the observed tier drops
    the capture clause, and a repo that set checkpoint_push_remote is told
    nothing further, because repeating the key it already set reads as a
    warning that something still needs doing.
    
    The test asserts "no session history" absent alongside the two phrasings
    this note was previously wrong with, so the next rewrite cannot
    reintroduce any of the three.

The trail page itself is a client-rendered SPA, so WebFetch got only the shell — I reviewed the underlying commit locally instead (`6c71f739b`, the tip of this branch).

## Verdict

The change is correct and an improvement. I verified the premise it rests on: capture's proposal genuinely runs *above* the single-remote gate (`strategy/manual_commit_push.go:83-101`, `pendingCapture` passed into `checkpointSyncAllowedForRemote`), so the old "carries your code but no session history" line was indeed false for the one push that matters — the electing one. Removing it and naming the destination instead is the right call. Asking `ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` rather than re-reading `checkpoint_push_remote` matches the `pinned`/`CoreOrigin()` rule already established in this file.

Checks: `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean, and `TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` passes (4.3s).

## Findings

**1. The fail-closed case now says nothing — and it's the case that most needs saying** (`remote_topology.go:107`, `:210`)

`inspectRemoteTopology` drops the resolver error into a debug log, so `syncRemote` is empty and `describeSyncRemote` returns silently. But inside that call site there are always ≥2 remotes, and with ≥2 remotes a successful resolve *never* returns an empty name (the origin/first tiers always yield one). So `syncRemote == ""` there means exactly one thing: `checkpoint_push_remote` names a missing remote and checkpoint sync is **disabled**. `entire status` reports that (`status.go:280-288` keeps the error in `checkpointSyncInfo.Err`), but the enable/doctor note doesn't even point at `entire status` in this branch — the user gets "This repo has 3 remotes (…)" and nothing else.

Keeping the error (or a bool) on `remoteTopology` and emitting one line — `Checkpoint sync is disabled: checkpoint_push_remote names a remote that does not exist. Run \`entire status\`.` — costs three lines and closes the gap. The doc comment's rationale ("naming a destination the push side would not use") argues against naming a remote, which is right; it doesn't argue for silence.

**2. Two of the three new branches are untested**

There's no `remote_topology_test.go`, and the integration test only exercises the default tier (`right now "origin"`). `SyncRemoteSourceConfig` and `SyncRemoteSourceObserved` — the two branches whose whole point is *different* wording — have no coverage. `describeSyncRemote` is a pure function of two fields writing to an `io.Writer`; a four-row table test (config / observed / default / empty) is cheap and would also pin the finding above once fixed.

**3. Comment says "Two phrasings", lists three** (`multi_pushurl_test.go:398`)

The `absent` slice has three entries and the comment enumerates three. Just a stale count.

**4. Minor, pre-existing: the observed-tier wording can go stale**

`"backup", your branch's push destination` describes the *captured* remote, and capture sticks — first still-configured capture wins. Re-point the branch afterwards and the note asserts something no longer true. It matches what `entire status` already says, so this isn't introduced here, but "your branch's push destination" is doing more work in a declarative sentence than in status's "follows…" framing.

Nothing blocking. #1 is the one I'd fix before merge.

All three findings are fixed, plus one the linter surfaced along the way. Tree is uncommitted.

**1. Fail-closed election now speaks** (`remote_topology.go`)

`remoteTopology` keeps the resolver error in a new `syncErr` field instead of dropping it into a debug log, and `describeSyncRemote` emits one line when the name is empty:

```
  This repo has 2 remotes (backup, origin).
    Checkpoints are NOT syncing: checkpoint_push_remote "gone" is not a configured git remote; checkpoint sync disabled until fixed
```

Wording mirrors `entire status`'s "Checkpoints NOT syncing" so the two surfaces read as the same fact. No destination is ever named on this path. The field comment carries the reasoning that makes the branch sound — with ≥2 remotes a successful election always yields a name, so an empty name there can only mean fail-closed — and the function doc notes this is the one branch that is a warning rather than orientation.

**2. `remote_topology_test.go`** — new table test over `describeSyncRemote`: config, observed, open-election, fail-closed, and nothing-resolved. Each row asserts both the text that must appear and the text that must not (no `Set strategy_options` on the already-pinned tier, no `right now` on a settled one, no destination named on the fail-closed one, no `no session history` anywhere).

**3.** "Two phrasings" → "Three phrasings" in the integration test comment.

**4. `exhaustive` lint failure that was already on the branch** — `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=main` flagged the `switch t.syncSource` for using `default` instead of naming `SyncRemoteSourceDefault`, `Sole`, and `First`. CI would have failed on the commit as it stood. Now listed explicitly, which also documents that the "a push can still take it over" wording is deliberately the shared text for all three open tiers.

## The problem

The several-remotes note printed by `entire enable` / `entire doctor` says:

> Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote — not to whichever one you push to. **A push to any other remote carries your code but no session history.** Run `entire status` to see the elected destination and how many checkpoints are waiting for it.

That bolded sentence is not true of the one push that matters most. `pendingCaptureCheckpointSyncRemote` runs **before** the single-remote gate in `prePush`, so a push whose target agrees with the branch's declared push destination elects that remote *and* carries the checkpoints there in the same push (`TestCheckpointSyncRemote_TrackedPushCapturesElection` asserts exactly that). The note was warning about a case the CLI now handles by itself.

It also never said where checkpoints actually go — the one thing a user standing in a multi-remote repo wants to know.

## The change

`inspectRemoteTopology` asks `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` for the election (never re-derived from settings — the same rule the existing `pinned` field follows, so the shown destination cannot diverge from where pushes go), and the note says the concrete thing. Election still open:

```
  This repo has 3 remotes (custom, origin, upstream).
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — right now "origin", and your first push to
    your branch's own remote takes it over. `entire status` shows where.
    Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin one yourself.
```

Observed tier — destination settled, capture clause gone:

```
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — "custom", your branch's push destination.
    Set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to pin a different one.
```

Explicit `checkpoint_push_remote` — one line, no advice, because repeating the key they already set reads as a warning that something still needs doing:

```
    Checkpoints sync to one remote — "custom" (set by checkpoint_push_remote).
```

The fan-out block above (one remote, several push URLs) is untouched — that one is still genuinely lossy.

## Test

`TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` now asserts `"no session history"` **absent**, alongside the two phrasings this note was already wrong with (`"follow whichever remote"`, `"always looks at origin"`), so a future rewrite cannot reintroduce any of the three.

## Verification

- `mise run lint` clean.
- `TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` and `TestCheckpointSyncRemote*` pass.
- All three states verified by hand against a 3-remote repo.
- `mise run test:ci` did **not** pass end to end locally: `cmd/entire/cli/agentimport` and `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch` time out (~600s, a test hanging on a spawned subprocess). Both reproduce on pristine `origin/main` in the same scratch worktree, so they are pre-existing/environmental and unrelated to this change — but they mean the local full-suite signal is incomplete, and CI is the real check.
